subject: transects or grids; set start manually; model.average()

messages.author: 4bfae3793264e847
messages.subject: transects or grids; set start manually; model.average()
parts:
Dear secr community,

I am trying to estimate population densities for a neotropical rodent species that I captured in several independent sites and have a bunch of different questions. I hope the structure of my post (f.e. several unrelated questions at once) is allright. If you prefer independent posts for each topic please let me know!

1.Comparability between sites:
I would like to compare population densities for on species that was captured in different habitat types (we have several replicas per habitat type). Due to topography, size and form of habitat patches, it was difficult to standardize the trapping design for all habitat types. The distance between trapping stations was generally the same for all habitat types but the overall design differed between them: transect pairs or trapping grids.
My question is whether I will produce biased density estimates because the trapping design differs between habitat types.


2. Set start manually:
For most of my capture sites secr.fit works well with different model specifications
secrAS51 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~1, mask = AS5.mask, method = "BFGS")
secrAS52 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~b , mask = AS5.mask, method = "BFGS")
secrAS53 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = AS5.mask, method = "BFGS")
secrAS55 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~b+T, mask = AS5.mask, method = "BFGS")

(the only model that almost never works out is g0 ~ h2; I used method = "BFGS" because it was resulting in much less error messages than either Newton-Raphson or Nelder-Mead )

For some sites secr.fit only works if I set the start manually. However, I am having doubts about specifiying the starting values for D, g0 and sigma. Can I infer these values from my capture data e.g. N of individuals divided by the area of the habitat mask as an approximation for D? For sigma I can imagine the minimum home range size as being a good starting point.

3. model average()
As mentioned above several models run well. For model.average() I read the recommendation based on Turek and Fletcher (2012) in the secr manual to use AIC instead of AICc. However, the SE estimate using criterion = AICc seems more "realistic" (I do not want to use the word "better") than the SE estimate that I get when using criterion = AIC (see below)

model.average(secrAS51, secrAS52, secrAS53, secrAS55, realnames = NULL, betanames = NULL,
alpha = 0.05, dmax = 10, covar = FALSE, average = "real",
criterion = "AIC", CImethod = "Wald")

        estimate SE.estimate          lcl         ucl
D      4.5839589  40.1277902  0.076827326 273.5052785
g0     0.0869694   0.1049543  0.007091151   0.5595572
sigma 28.5644831   6.3475692 18.575818476  43.9242930

for criterion = AICc
         estimate SE.estimate         lcl        ucl
D      2.35663989  0.89970741  1.14370613  4.8559253
g0     0.02611265  0.01029052  0.01198583  0.0559469
sigma 28.67187765  0.68973787 27.35157746 30.0559106

Any recommendations which criterion I should use?

Thank you very much for investing your time in reading this long post! I am greatful for any help!

All the best,
Julian

Sorry, for sigma I did not mean the minimum home range size but the radius around a trap where an animal was captured and this radius may be derived from the minimum home range size

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: transects or grids; set start manually; model.average()
parts:
Hello Julian, and welcome to the group

1. If your animals are behaving according to the model, and you have adequate data (not too sparse, traps not too far apart) then different trapping designs should all produce unbiased estimates. There is a potential problem with parallel transects if animals have home ranges elongated systematically in one direction with respect to the transects; elongation is almost certainly _not_ a problem with layouts that don't have a strong 'grain' (e.g., square grids). So there is a potential effect of layout on estimates in that case.

2. I'm surprised g0~h2 'almost never works' if you are using the default detection function detectfn = 0 or 'HN' - I wonder what causes that? Regarding start values: you are free to use whatever works for you. For sigma I suggest 0.2 times the sqrt of the home range area in sq. metres (or the home range radius / 2.5). The simplest form for the start values is a list of real parameter values like: start = list(D=1, g0=0.2, sigma=25). You may also find it convenient to pass the name of a previously fitted model (secr.fit will find the values it needs).

3. Something has gone seriously wrong with the model averaging using AIC (D-hat 4.6, SE 40.1!). Do you have a reason to override the default for 'average' (averaging on the link scale)? That is the scale on which the SE really 'make sense'. If the problem persists, and isn't just due to a really strange model, I'm going to have to look at the code, which may not happen for a few days.

Hope this is some use
Murray

messages.subject: Re: transects or grids; set start manually; model.average()
parts:
Hello Murray,

thanks! It was definitely help!
g0~h2 'almost never works' means that in most cases I received the warning: at least one variance calculation failed.

2. I did not change the settings for "average" on purpose, that was an accident. Changing it to the default "link" however, did not alter much in the results, yet for some sites SE got a little bit smaller.
In some cases, this happens only when I set the start manually,

secrPB.ed1 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.PB.ed, model = g0~1, mask = PB.ed.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma = 17), method = "BFGS")
secrPB.ed2 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.PB.ed, model = g0~b , mask = PB.ed.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma = 17), method = "BFGS")
secrPB.ed3 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.PB.ed, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = PB.ed.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma = 17), method = "BFGS")
secrPB.ed5 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.PB.ed, model = g0~b+T, mask = PB.ed.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma = 17), method = "BFGS")

After applying model.average() I still get really strange estimates for D and SE, which as you mentioned could be due to sparse data (1 recapture in 10 detections). Strangely enough, the same settings work for other sites with the same trap outlay but with even less data.  
Thanks again for your help!
Julian
